thread:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER: High error rate from eu-west and eu-central customers — surge in 5xxs and a spike in cross-region routing to us-east. Maria is currently on-call. Incident ID: INC-2026-4943 :rotating_light:

maria: seeing it in the dashboard, thanks. can someone confirm whether this is routing policy related or backend capacity?

kevin: checking model-serving pools — no obvious capacity pressure in eu region. token latency is normal for group-eu. 5xxs look like 502/504 from our edge proxies.

lia: telemetry: geo-steer signal shows sudden weight flip to us-east for ~30% of eu traffic starting 00:12 UTC. TTLs look normal but policy eval logs show ABORT on region-pin rule eval. grabbing eval logs.

maria: @tariq can you check the routing control plane? if policy evals are aborting maybe a rollout or operator change hit the pinning operator.

incidents-bot: New incident created: Cross-region routing misroute (INC-2026-4943). Severity: P1. Channels: #incidents, #eng-networking, #oncall-escalations.

tariq: looking at the control plane, there was a canary rollout of a new pinning policy at 00:10 UTC that targeted 'eu-*' with a fallback fallback-to-region set. Canary completed but a buggy guard clause caused null pointer in the pin-resolver which returned empty region, causing downstream fallthrough to weight-based steering.

maria: that would explain the sudden weight flip. can we revert the canary?

kevin: yes, I'm rolling the policy back now. command:```
# rollback canary
redwoodctl routing-policy rollback --policy-id policy-ctx-9834 --to-revision 4
```

lia: telemetry: starting to see decrease in misrouted requests after rollback command issued. still seeing queued requests hitting us-east.

maria: mitigation step 1: rollback applied. step 2: temporarily pin eu geofence at the edge to enforce strict region affinity for authenticated customers to stop user-impact. Tariq can you push edge pin?

tariq: pushing the edge pin now:```
# apply edge override
redwood-edgectl pin --geofence eu --force --reason "emergency stopgap for INC-2026-4943"
```

incidents-bot: Edge override applied by tariq. Duration: 15m (auto-expire).

customer-ops: getting customer reports from a handful of EU production tenants — timeouts around 00:13-00:20 UTC, affecting sync APIs. severity reported: degraded UX but no data loss. we should prepare customer communication.

maria: lia please prepare initial incident banner with impact: "EU customers experienced higher error rates and increased latency due to cross-region routing misroutes; mitigated via rollback and temporary edge pin. Investigating root cause."

lia: banner drafted and sent to status page: "We rolled back a routing policy canary and applied temporary region pins to mitigate misrouting. Services are recovering — some requests may still see errors."

kevin: verifying replicates: we see <1% of traffic still misrouted due to DNS caches honoring previous weights (TTL 60). we can force a lower TTL and nuke PDNS caches, but that will be disruptive. options: 1) wait ~2 TTL cycles, 2) nuke caches globally, 3) add explicit header to edge that forces origin selection — risky. Thoughts?

maria: go with wait for 2 cycles for now, but nuke if errors don't drop under 0.5% in 10 minutes. lia, keep watch.

lia: monitoring: 5xx rate dropped from 4.8% -> 0.9% at +3 minutes post-rollback. latency for eu users reduced from 480ms median -> 220ms. keeping eyes on it.

tariq: root cause evidence: policy-resolver service logs show NPE in the latest canary revision when a geo tag was empty. fallback behavior returned empty region and allowed weighted steering to take effect. will open a fix PR to harden the resolver.

maria: good. assign owners: tariq + kevin on remediation, lia on monitoring + comms, myself on postmortem. set a bridge for 00:40 UTC for RCA sync.

incidents-bot: @maria set severity -> P1, conference bridge created: 10.0.0.45:3489.

customer-ops: customers we notified confirmed improvements after the rollback. one enterprise tenant reported three failed jobs during the 8-minute window. offering follow-up support.

kevin: deploying a small validation in policy-resolver to explicitly reject empty geo-tags rather than nulling. PR:```https://git.internal/r/redwood/policy-resolver/pull/322``` will be hotpatched after the incident.

lia: auto-expire for edge-pin is at +12 minutes. recommending extend to 30m until DNS caches settle. Maria?

maria: extend to 30m. tariq please monitor for any routing churn after extension.

tariq: extended. also adding temporary alert suppression for noisy downstream alerts tied to weight flips to avoid pager storms.

lia: note on customer impact summary for postmortem: ~12 tenants affected, peak error window 00:12-00:20 UTC, median additional latency +250ms, approximate affected request volume ~18k requests globally, EU misroute volume ~4.2k.

maria: thanks. timeline so far: 00:10 canary rollout -> 00:12 error spike -> 00:14 pager -> 00:16 rollback -> 00:18 edge pin -> 00:22 error rates sub-1% -> 00:40 bridge for RCA.

incidents-bot: Reminder: please add all incident-related artifacts (logs, dashboards, PR links) to INC-2026-4943 ticket.

maria: post-incident actions: 1) revert canary permanently until extra validation added, 2) add stricter preflight for geo-tag presence, 3) change default fallback region behavior to explicit deny, 4) update runbook to include edge-pin as mitigation, 5) comms to affected customers. I'll assign owners in the incident tracker.

customer-ops: CS follow-ups scheduled for tomorrow morning for affected enterprise customers.

kevin: hotpatch PR merged to canary-fix branch. rolling a safe patch to policy-resolver with extra unit tests. will coordinate with tariq for staged rollout.

lia: closing notes in thread: monitoring remains green, edge pin auto-extended to 30m and will expire at 00:48 UTC. liaison for postmortem is maria. any objections to declaring mitigated?

tariq: no objections. marking mitigated but keeping incident open for RCA until root cause fix is in prod.

maria: mitigated. opening follow-up ticket for RCA and scheduled postmortem doc. thanks all for rapid response. :clap:
